data.title: Nike eyes cricket as a way to grow sales in India aggressively
data.description:
Nike is shifting some of its global priorities to target the high-growth sports market in India. The athletic apparel company has a goal to triple its business in India in just five years.

The company is investing to build its portfolio of running, training, and sportswear products in the country. An area of emphasis will be cricket, where Nike plans to expand offerings, support grassroots programs, and add partnerships. Nike has already partnered with the billionaire Mukesh Ambani-owned Mumbai Indians team and set plans to open a new campus in India.

Of note, India's athletic footwear and apparel market is estimated at $9B and is projected to grow over 10% annually to roughly $14B by 2030–2031.

Shares of Nike were up 1.5% in late Wednesday trading.

data.title: Dow Industrials Slide After Nvidia's Results Fail to Ease Worries — WSJ
data.description:
By Alexander Osipovich

Nvidia's blockbuster earnings failed to give tech stocks a lift, a sign that worries about the AI trade continue to haunt investors after days of drama over the chip maker's ousted CEO Jensen Huang.

The Dow is in the red, while the Nasdaq turned higher in the last hour. Nvidia shares are slipping despite the company posting another quarter of record revenue and upgraded guidance. The stock has lost more than a third of its value since early last month.

Other AI-linked stocks such as CoreWeave are down, but have pared losses. Investors will now turn to the next big test for the AI trade: Anthropic's mega-IPO, expected tomorrow.

Oil prices are falling as data showing growing U.S. inventories overshadow the latest flare-up of fighting in the Persian Gulf.

Fed governor Christopher Waller reiterated his call for a half-percentage point rate hike in December. Central bank minutes released at 2 p.m. ET did little to change traders' views that a rate hike is likely in December.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Customer Loyalty Has Limits: Most Would Shop With a Competitor During an Unexpected Closure, Survey Finds
data.description:
The Hanover's 2026 Small Business Pulse Report highlights growing consumer expectations around trust, business continuity and employee safety

WORCESTER, Mass., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- According to new research by The Hanover Insurance Group, Inc. () and Statista, 60% of respondents would temporarily shop with a competitor if their preferred small business closed due to an unexpected event, with more than half seeking alternatives within a week.

The Hanover's 2026 Small Business Pulse Report: Reputation, Risk and Resilience examines the factors that most influence small business shoppers' trust and the events most likely to damage a business's reputation. Its findings underscore the role preparedness, employee safety and risk management play in helping small businesses maintain trust. The research found reliable products and services, protection of customer data, transparent communication and fair treatment of employees are among the factors respondents identify as most important in earning trust.

"Our research shows 87% of respondents say small businesses are important to their communities and 61% shop at a small business at least once a week," said Charles (Chip) F. Hamann, president of small commercial at The Hanover. "At the same time, the survey also underscores the importance of customer data protection, employee safety and business preparedness in earning and maintaining trust among consumers. Small businesses that proactively manage risk can strengthen customer confidence and position themselves to recover more effectively when disruptions occur. An independent agent is well positioned to help business owners navigate evolving risks, strengthen preparedness strategies and identify insurance solutions that support long-term resilience."

Trust extends beyond products and services

While reliable products and services remain the foundation of customer trust, the survey also explored other factors that may shape confidence in a business. When asked to rank the events that would be most likely to damage their trust in a small business, respondents most often placed the following among their top three:

  • Serious product safety issues (73%)
  • Customer data or privacy breaches (73%)
  • Employee safety or workplace treatment (69%)

Respondents also ranked the factors that were most important in earning their trust. Sixty-eight percent ranked reliable products and services in their top three factors. Protecting customer data followed with 62%. Lastly, transparent communication when problems occurred and treating employees fairly were among the top three factors for 54% of respondents.

Employee safety strengthens reliability

Respondents also associated employee safety with a greater likelihood of business success. Ninety-two percent of respondents agree small businesses that invest in employee safety are more likely to provide reliable service and remain successful over time. The finding suggests small business shoppers view employee safety as an indicator of operational stability and responsible business management.

To learn more about the findings from The Hanover's 2026 Small Business Pulse Report: Reputation, Risk and Resilience, visit hanover.com. For more information on The Hanover's small business insurance solutions, please visit hanover.com/businesses.

About the survey

The online survey was conducted by Statista+ on behalf of The Hanover from Sept. 2-4, 2026, among 500 U.S. consumers ages 18 to 64 who purchase products or services from small businesses at least once a month. For ranking questions, "top three" represents the percentage of respondents who placed a factor first, second or third.

About The Hanover

The Hanover Insurance Group, Inc. is the holding company for several property and casualty insurance companies, which together constitute one of the largest insurance businesses in the United States. The company provides exceptional insurance solutions through a select group of independent agents and brokers. Together with its agent partners, The Hanover offers standard and specialized insurance protection for small and mid-sized businesses, as well as for homes, automobiles, and other personal items. data.title: SOLV Energy raised to Buy at UBS after strong backlog growth
data.description:
SOLV Energy rose 0.9% in Wednesday's trading as UBS upgraded the power industry infrastructure services provider to Buy from Neutral with a $37 price target, saying the market is underappreciating some key tailwinds given the current uncertainty around data center demand and higher interest rates.

SOLV shares peaked at ~$47, up 87% from the February 2026 IPO price of $25, but they have since dropped back to roughly the original IPO price despite two acquisitions, beating and raising guidance in Q2 and Q3 and raising backlog 37% Y/Y to $9.2B since the IPO, providing an attractive entry point for investors, UBS analyst Jon Windham said.

The analyst also noted M&A upside potential, with continued expansion into adjacent services broadening SOLV's scope of work and supporting earnings growth, and that the U.S. midterm election likely provides a Senate firewall to protect support for clean energy, resulting in a renewed focus on non-polluting energy sources for data center development.

data.title: Federal Jury Indicts Russian National on Charges of Spying on Defense Company
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D'iu, a Russian national, on charges he was spying on a U.S. defense-technology firm, according to the Justice Department.

The federal charges allege D'iu conspired to act and acted as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the U.S. Attorney General. He is also charged with interstate stalking and fraud in connection with identification documents, according to the DOJ.

The charges are all related to an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology-defense company, the DOJ said.

D'iu entered the U.S. illegally this summer at the direction of foreign handlers to gather information about the defense company, according to the indictment and affidavit. He received instructions and support from others through the messaging platform Telegram, the documents say.

D'iu wasn't immediately available for comment, and it wasn't clear whether he had legal representation.

The company was allegedly targeted because of its assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia, Craig Missakian, U.S. attorney for the Northern District of California, said.

D'iu had his initial appearance in federal court on Nov. 2 and has remained in federal custody since, the DOJ said. He is set to appear in federal court on Nov. 24, the DOJ added.

If convicted, D'iu faces up to five years in prison for conspiracy and 10 years in prison for acting as a foreign agent, according to the DOJ. He could get up to one year in prison for fraud in connection with identification documents, the agency said. Fines could total as much as $600,000, the DOJ said.

data.title: Fed’s Daly Emphasizes Need For Rate Hikes, But With A ‘Measured Approach’ As Fed Minutes Show Growing Inflation Unease
data.description:
Key points:
  • Daly urged officials to proceed cautiously while monitoring economic data and ongoing uncertainties. 
  • Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller warned that persistent price pressures may require a larger 50-basis-point increase in December.
  • Markets have entirely priced in a 25-basis-point hike in December. 

Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said Wednesday that further interest rate hikes will be required to ensure inflation returns to the central bank's 2% target.

However, Daly suggested policymakers should adopt a “measured pace” and evaluate shifting economic conditions.

Speaking during a virtual conversation at a St. Louis Fed conference, Daly highlighted that economic uncertainty remains elevated. She pointed to unresolved questions surrounding future tariff policies, geopolitical conflict involving Iran, and massive capital expenditures tied to the artificial intelligence boom.

"This measured approach we've been taking, and I would be supportive of continuing to take, is the right way to go," Daly said, emphasizing the importance of evaluating incoming data and listening closely to consumers and businesses.

Fed Minutes Show Rate Hikes In Favor

A majority of Federal Reserve officials agreed on the need to raise interest rates “in the months ahead” to return inflation to their 2% target in a timely manner during the October rate-setting meeting.

According to minutes published Wednesday from the Federal Open Market Committee's October 27-28 session, officials noted that a rate hike exceeding 25 basis points might become necessary at the December gathering should future inflation metrics deteriorate further.

“In the months ahead, almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate,” the minutes said, “would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective.”

Christopher Waller Calls For Aggressive Action

Echoing a more hawkish tone, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller argued that the central bank may need to deliver a larger-than-usual 50-basis-point (half-percentage-point) increase at its upcoming December policy meeting.

“You have to go 50 in December to put it in place and get it done,” Waller told CNBC's Steve Liesman during an interview. “I'm very concerned about inflation. It's headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out.”

While some officials share Waller's urgency for larger moves or consecutive quarter-point adjustments, others favor a slower, data-dependent approach. Meanwhile, derivatives markets continue to price in standard quarter-point bumps at the December and January meetings.

data.title: Lowe's 3Q Sales Rise, as Professional Customers Drive Growth — Update
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Lowe's reported higher sales in the recent quarter, largely driven by growth in its business selling to professional customers.

Profit climbed as well, thanks to a large tariff refund the home-improvement retailer said it plans to reinvest in the business. Still, Lowe's maintained its earnings outlook for the year and said higher costs are weighing on margins.

Shares fell premarket but pared their losses and were roughly flat in afternoon trading.

Chief Executive Marvin Ellison on Wednesday said professional customers are responding well to enhancements Lowe's has made to its fulfillment network. At the same time, loyalty offerings are helping the company to deepen customer relationships and capture more spend.

Third-quarter net sales climbed 9.3% to $22.76 billion, just ahead of Wall Street estimates for $22.39 billion. Growth across Lowe's professional business--as well as its home-services unit and online sales channels--helped offset softer trends across the company's do-it-yourself business.

There are some green shoots, though. For instance, Lowe's logged its strongest quarter of appliance sales in five years, Ellison said on a call with analysts.

"That says a lot when you think about the pressure that the DIY consumer is under," he added.

Lowe's results echo those of rival Home Depot, which also reported higher sales and profit in the latest quarter, helped by strength among professional contractors despite continued weakness in the broader home-improvement market.

Lowe's said comparable sales, which account for store openings and closings, climbed 1.8% for the three months ended Oct. 30, ahead of analyst views for a 0.1% gain. Higher average tickets, which in part reflected inflation in commodity-driven categories such as lumber and electrical cable, offset a decline in comparable transactions, Chief Financial Officer Brandon Sink said.

For the year, Lowe's now expects same-store sales to tick up 0.5%, whereas they were previously expected to be flat.

Profit climbed to $1.67 billion, from $1.62 billion a year earlier. Adjusted earnings came in at $3.10 a share, including a 34-cent benefit tied to tariff refunds. Analysts were looking for adjusted earnings of $2.88 a share.

Excluding the tariff refund, Lowe's said its bottom line was pressured by recent acquisitions, as well as elevated fuel and transportation costs. Productivity initiatives spanning merchandising, stores, supply chain and corporate functions are helping to offset that pressure, Sink said.

Lowe's reinvested about a third of its $250 million tariff refund back into the business during the third quarter, and the company expects to reinvest the remainder during the fourth.

"Our intention is to reinvest our tariff refunds in ways that strengthen our customer value proposition by putting these dollars to work to enhance the customer experience, strengthen our competitive position, and bring value to our customers," Ellison said.

For the year, Lowe's continues to expect earnings of about $11.25 a share, or about $12.25 a share on an adjusted basis.

Write to Connor Hart at connor.hart@wsj.com

data.title: Southern California port employers say no movement on watchmen contract talks as strike risk grows
data.description:
Key points:
  • ILWU Local 26 signals no contract extension beyond 12:01 a.m. Saturday, PMA says
  • Watchmen have already voted to authorize strike at US's busiest container port complex
  • PMA offer includes $3,200 bonus and average full-time pay raise of 16% to $198,000

By Lisa Baertlein

The Pacific Maritime Association (PMA) employers group at the Los Angeles and Long Beach seaports on Wednesday said its latest negotiation session with 250 watchmen represented by the International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) ended with "little-to-no movement from the union on PMA’s proposals."

PMA said ILWU Local 26 has indicated an unwillingness to extend the contract beyond its expiration at 12:01 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, setting the stage for a potential strike at the nation’s busiest container cargo port complex that could disrupt operations at a time when volumes are running at record levels.

The ILWU watchmen, who already have voted to authorize a strike, did not immediately comment. They account for roughly 2% of union workers at the port complex, but their work is critical because they verify identification and credentials at terminal access points, conduct security patrols and report safety issues.

The PMA said its offer includes a one-time bonus of $3,200 for each member and a wage proposal that would raise average annual earnings for full-time watchmen from more than $170,000 to $198,000. The offer also would maintain fully employer-paid healthcare for active workers and retirees, valued at more than $62,000 each year, and increase pension benefits up to $93,200 a year for workers with the longest tenure.

The talks have stretched on for more than a year, with the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service recently stepping in to assist. PMA said Local 26’s demands have not materially changed since negotiations began.

The PMA and 22,000 ILWU dockworkers at ports along the US West Coast in 2023 hammered out a separate, six-year labor deal following intervention from former President Joe Biden's acting secretary of labor. That averted a strike at the ports, which handle around 40% of US container imports.

In 2024, nearly 50,000 International Longshoremen's Association dockworkers hit an impasse with employers at three dozen ports on the US East Coast and Gulf Coast over wage increases and port automation. The union workers' crippling three-day strike shut down shipping to those gateways, resulting in the biggest work stoppage of its kind in nearly half a century.

data.title: Pain in TQQQ, SOXL may offer silver lining for tech stocks - SocGen
data.description:
Investors in the largest U.S. triple-leveraged technology exchange-traded funds have nearly erased tens of billions of dollars in 2026 paper profits, even as the underlying unleveraged funds remain solidly positive for the year, according to data from Societe Generale Cross Asset Research.

Aggregate 2026 investor profit and loss on the ProShares UltraPro QQQ ETF and the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF —which offer 3x leveraged exposure to the Nasdaq-100 and semiconductors , respectively—has fallen back to roughly breakeven in November.

At their mid-year peaks around late June and July, SocGen noted, cumulative investor gains had reached roughly $17B for TQQQ and almost $40B for SOXL before an autumn selloff wiped out the advances.

With daily leverage resetting compound losses during choppy swings, TQQQ and SOXL holders now sit near flat on the year while their unleveraged underlying ETFs remain up some 7.5% and 40% year-to-date.

Still, strategists noted that the washout could signal a contrarian silver lining for U.S. tech stocks . When aggregate capital invested in Korean leveraged single-stock ETFs tipped into losses at the end of July, that inflection point marked a local bottom for the underlying shares—a pattern SocGen thinks is now worth watching in U.S. technology.

data.title: Crude Oil Plummeting As Inventories Increase More Than Expected
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After partly offsetting Monday's nosedive in the previous session, the price of crude oil has shown a substantial move back to the downside during trading on Wednesday.

Crude oil for December has regained some ground after plummeting early in the day but is still sharply lower, plunging $2.92 or 3.4 percent to $83.09 a barrel.

The price of crude oil has more than offset the modest increase seen on Tuesday, tumbling to its lowest levels in over two months.

Selling pressure resurfaced following the release of a report from the Energy Information Administration showing U.S. crude oil inventories increased by much more than expected in the week ended November 13th.

The EIA said crude oil inventories climbed by 3.4 million barrels last week after jumping by 4.7 million barrels in the previous week. Economists had expected crude oil inventories to inch up by 0.4 million barrels.

At 417.8 million barrels, U.S. crude oil inventories are still 3 percent below the five-year average for this time of year, the report said.

The EIA said gasoline inventories also shot up by 5.2 million barrels last week, while distillate inventories, which include heating oil and diesel, also rose by 1.6 million barrels.

Oversupply concerns have recently outweighed geopolitical risks after the International Energy Agency said the world oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year on the back of recovering Middle East exports.

Meanwhile, American warplanes hit an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf on Tuesday in response to aggression by the IRGC targeting U.S. service members and assets, a U.S. military official said.

Iran Army's Navy said a fourth tanker violating regulations set in place by Tehran has struck a naval mine and caught fire in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Malibu Boats Launches Response TXi Worlds Preview Ahead of the 2027 IWWF World Waterski Championships
data.description:
LOUDON, Tenn., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Malibu Boats, Inc. , the global leader in performance sport boats, today announced the Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview, a global series of familiarization events that gives waterskiers the opportunity to get behind the Response TXi with AtmosDrive and experience the boat before competing on it. Running from December 2026 through February 2027, the series stops in Florida, along Australia’s east coast, and at the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships site in Peru.

As the exclusive official towboat partner of the International Waterski & Wakeboard Federation (IWWF), Malibu will tow all IWWF World Waterski Championships with the Response TXi with AtmosDrive, including the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships in Peru (Jan. 10–16, 2027), the 2027 IWWF World Waterski Championships in Australia (Feb. 16–21, 2027), and the 2028 IWWF World Over 35 Waterski Championships (Aug. 27–Sept. 3, 2028). The Worlds Preview gives athletes from every nation the chance to ski behind the boat well before they reach the start dock.

Having pulled 13 world records in waterskiing, the Response TXi is built on Malibu’s T-Cut Diamond Hull, allowing it to track precisely and leave a minimal wake. AtmosDrive delivers more of the engine’s pull into every set: jumpers feel it at the ramp, while slalom and trick skiers feel it through every pass. Many of the world’s top skiers have yet to ski behind the Response TXi, and the Worlds Preview is designed to change that by bringing the boat within reach before competition.

In the United States, the series arrives Dec. 18–20 with a three-day event at Champions Lake in Auburndale, Florida. Athletes from every IWWF member federation can ski timed sets in slalom, trick, and jump, with Will Asher joining Malibu representatives and event staff on the dock throughout the event.

In Australia, Malibu Boats Australia brings the Worlds Preview to four venues across Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland from Dec. 10 through Jan. 22, with priority for Australian Open and U21 team members. Sessions run at Bridgewater, Victoria (Dec. 10–11); Albury, New South Wales (Dec. 18 and 21–22); Marshalls, Queensland (Jan. 14–15), and Stoney Park, New South Wales (Jan. 18–19), with Australian Masters familiarization at Bridgewater on Jan. 22. The same boat will also tow three L-rated tournaments: the Bridgewater Malibu Series, the Albury Jump-Off, and the Australian Masters. For the two weeks before the Worlds, Feb. 1–5 and 8–12, the boat and site at Albury are open to competitors from every nation.

In Peru, two Response TXi boats with AtmosDrive will be at Bujama Lacus, site of the 2027 IWWF World Under 21 Waterski Championships (Jan. 10–16, 2027), for official familiarization Jan. 10–12, ahead of preliminary rounds beginning Jan. 13.

Official familiarization and competition will be towed by:

Brand: Malibu

Model: Response TXi

Engine: Monsoon M6Di 430 HP (6.2 Liter)

Transmission: ZF 1.22:1

Speed Control: Zero Off, latest version

Slalom & Trick Prop: OJ 3090 – 4 Blade – 14 × 14

Jump Prop: OJ 3084 – 3 Blade – 14 × 13

“The work that happens before competition matters,” said Rachael Green, General Manager of Malibu Boats. “The TXi is built to give athletes the consistent pull and performance they need to focus on their skiing when it counts. The Worlds Preview gives skiers the chance to experience that performance firsthand and understand what makes the Response TXi a strong competition platform.”

“Confidence in the boat is what lets you push the limits,” added Will Asher, Malibu Pro Team skier. “I worked with our engineers on AtmosDrive so the pull would be something skiers can count on, pass after pass. When you trust the boat, you stop thinking about it and start chasing what’s possible. I’ll be on the dock in Florida to help skiers find that feeling for themselves.”

“The world is coming to Australian water, and the skiers deserve to know this boat long before it counts,” said Noel Gordon, Manufacturing & Process Engineer at Malibu Boats Australia. “From Bridgewater to Stoney Park, our Open and U21 teams will have the chance to log real sets behind the Response TXi all summer. Then, for the final two weeks, we open Albury to skiers from every nation, so when they reach the start dock, the boat already feels like home.”

The Worlds Preview underscores Malibu’s commitment to athlete development and to advancing waterskiing at every level, worldwide. More Malibu Response TXi Worlds Preview events are to come, and Malibu will announce them once they are planned.

A leading innovator in the powerboat industry, Malibu Boats, Inc. designs products for a growing range of recreational boaters, fishermen, and watersports enthusiasts who make boating a central part of their active lifestyles. data.title: Federal Jury Indicts Russian National on Charges of Spying on Defense Company
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D'iu, a Russian national, on charges he was spying on a U.S. defense-technology firm, according to the Justice Department.

The federal charges allege D'iu conspired to act and acted as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the U.S. Attorney General. He is also charged with interstate stalking and fraud in connection with identification documents, according to the DOJ.

The charges are all related to an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology-defense company, the DOJ said.

D'iu entered the U.S. illegally this summer at the direction of foreign handlers to gather information about the defense company, according to the indictment and affidavit. He received instructions and support from others through the messaging platform Telegram, the documents say.

D'iu wasn't immediately available for comment, and it wasn't clear whether he had legal representation.

The company was allegedly targeted because of its assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia, Craig Missakian, U.S. attorney for the Northern District of California, said.

D'iu had his initial appearance in federal court on Nov. 2 and has remained in federal custody since, the DOJ said. He is set to appear in federal court on Nov. 24, the DOJ added.

If convicted, D'iu faces up to five years in prison for conspiracy and 10 years in prison for acting as a foreign agent, according to the DOJ. He could get up to one year in prison for fraud in connection with identification documents, the agency said. Fines could total as much as $600,000, the DOJ said.
